findings.message: This round moves the future-date bound for sync_proposal out of the `repoTime` zod transform and into `knownTime()`, called in `upsertSpecProposal` (createdAt) and `writeTasks` (doneAt). No test drives that write path with a future date. The only future-date tests are: the push path, which `desired()` already bounds before the write (repo-dates-094.test.ts:176, 283–285); the bare-helper table in ci-095.test.ts:13–20; and the sync_proposal created-date test, which sends only a past date (repo-dates-094.test.ts:231). Delete `knownTime` from services.ts:320 or tasks.ts:22 and every test stays green. Fix: add a table-driven test that calls `syncProposal` (or the `sync_proposal` MCP tool's run) on a proposal that already has stored dates. Rows: a future createdAt, a future task doneAt, and a past createdAt as the control. Assert the stored created_at and done_at are unchanged in the future rows.
findings.scenario: Remove `knownTime(...)` at services.ts:320 so the raw `input.createdAt` is written → sync_proposal with createdAt "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z" stores created_at = 2030-01-01 → the full delivery suite still passes.

findings.message: The new 095 mock's from-repo Released card (AMX-061) shows a single chip, "Released · from repo". The code renders two: ProjectPage.tsx:55 puts `p.release ?? "Released"` in the release chip slot, and line 66 adds the "Released · from repo" label chip, so the card reads "Released" next to "Released · from repo". The mock and the code disagree on that card. Either draw the mock as the code renders it, or (in a change that touches ProjectPage) leave out the fallback chip when there is no release.
findings.scenario: A specclaw proposal archived in the repo with no release → the board card shows the chips "Released" and "Released · from repo" → the mock shows only "Released · from repo".

findings.message: The 095 section sits under the `<!-- 094 sync repo dates and owner parser -->` banner comment, ahead of the 094 section it labels. It also has no data-roles, data-title, data-nav or data-parent attributes, which the sibling sections carry. Give it its own 095 banner and match the other sections' attributes.

The gate now credits a commit that names a `covered-by` change to its cover's final pass. AGENTS.md (Review scope) still says a later commit must name the covering change, or 'another change in the PR whose own final pass came after it'. A covered-by change has no final pass of its own, so the gate now accepts commits that the documented rule rejects. The code and the governance text disagree. Update the AGENTS.md sentence in this change to say a covered-by change is judged by its cover's final pass. The logic itself fails closed: the cover must be in the PR with a final pass, and the covered change is still judged on its own.
findings.scenario: A fork PR has 106-inner (covered-by 105-other) and a commit `specclaw(106-inner): code`, and 105-other's final pass comes after that commit. The gate passes. Read literally, AGENTS.md says it should fail, because 106-inner has no final pass of its own.

findings.message: This test calls `z.toJSONSchema` directly. Chat converts with `toolInputSchema` (packages/ai/src/tool-schema.ts). If that conversion ever changes (for example to `io: "input"` or added options), the two can disagree. The registry-wide `apps/web/tests/tool-schemas.test.ts` already runs `toolInputSchema` over every module's tools, so it already catches a transform in any module. Use `toolInputSchema(t.input)` here, or rely on the registry-wide test, so there is one definition of 'converts'.
findings.scenario: If toolInputSchema later converts with `{ io: "input" }`, a schema that throws only in output mode fails this test but works in chat (or the other way round).
